subject: Re: Renewal decision & third-party bakeoff — Stellarsys
messages:
From: Laura Myers <laura.myers@stellarsys.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@stellarsys.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal window + vendor bakeoff

Hi Kimberly,

StellarSys is entering our renewal window for the ML inference layer (July 2027). We received an inbound request from our CTO to run a short bakeoff against two other providers next month focused on latency at 95th percentile and cost-per-100k tokens at our steady-state traffic.

I've attached our bakeoff requirements (stellarsys_bakeoff_requirements.xlsx). Procurement is copied — they will coordinate logistics. Before we schedule anything, can you confirm:
- Whether Redwood can run an independent benchmark using our harness (we'll provide traffic profiles)
- If you can commit to a dedicated pool for the run and for a post-bakeout pilot if we choose Redwood
- Any minimum contract term required to access those commitments

The CTO is also pushing for comparable pricing to Vendor X in the event of replacement. Happy to jump on a quick call this week.

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Myers
VP, Platform Engineering
StellarSys

Attachment: stellarsys_bakeoff_requirements.xlsx

From: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Laura Myers <laura.myers@stellarsys.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal window + vendor bakeoff

Hi Laura — thanks for sending this over and for the heads-up on the bakeoff. We can absolutely run the benchmark against your harness. Quick answers up front:
- Benchmarking: yes — we can execute tests in your environment or spin a dedicated, isolated pool in our Dedicated product that mirrors your traffic. We prefer to run the canonical tests from the harness to ensure apples-to-apples.
- Dedicated pool: we can provision a temporary dedicated pool for the bakeoff and extend the same configuration for a pilot if you select Redwood.
- Minimum term: to offer the dedicated pool and pricing parity we usually ask for a 12-month committed term for Dedicated with a 3% onboarding credit; shorter terms are possible but require an uplift.

I'll loop in Rishi and Neha to scope the technical requirements and confirm resource sizing. Would you be open to a short technical sync tomorrow at 11am PT?

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 08:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal window + vendor bakeoff — bench plan

Kimberly / Neha —

Quick plan to prepare for the StellarSys run:
1) Environment: provision a three-node dedicated pool matching their peak concurrency (numbers in the workbook). We'll use the same model weights they specified; no fuzzing.
2) Test harness: import their traffic profile and run steady-state 2-hour windows + 30 min ramp. Measure p95 latency, p99 tail, and cost-per-100k tokens.
3) Metrics and docs: produce a short one-pager with token economics and a Grafana dashboard link; include binary artifacts and a log bundle for audit.
4) Contingencies: if we can't match p95 within 10% of Vendor X, propose fallback to a quantized variant that trades quality for cost savings (we'll include BLEU/QA checks).

Needs from sales: a negotiated term buffer. Procurement will ask for termination protections and credits if we miss SLA. Suggest we prepare a counter terms doc (Proposed Terms v3) with the following options: 12mo committed (preferred), 6mo (higher price), and a performance SLA addendum for the dedicated pool.

I can have the benchmark infra ready by Apr 20 if we get greenlight.

—Rishi
Lead Platform Engineer, Inference Runtime

Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal window + vendor bakeoff — terms & expectations

Kimberly —

Appreciate the quick coordination. Procurement has reviewed the ask and attached a redline of standard terms. Key asks from StellarSys:
- Pricing parity with Vendor X for steady-state (Vendor X provided a 10% lower token price at our expected volumes)
- A performance credit structure if p95 latency exceeds the agreed threshold during the first 90 days of production
- A commitment that Dedicated pool capacity will be available for at least 95% of peak traffic during business hours; otherwise, credits or fallback routing to a secondary provider.

We can sign an NDA if needed and will prioritize the bakeoff calendar once we have a firm offering. Attached: redlined_terms_stellarsys.docx (sent to procurement).

Jonas
Director, Procurement
StellarSys

Attachment: redlined_terms_stellarsys.docx

From: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Patel <jonas.patel@stellarsys.com>, Laura Myers <laura.myers@stellarsys.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 16:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal window + vendor bakeoff — Redwood counter and next steps

Jonas / Laura —

Thanks for the redline and for outlining the procurement asks. We want to be competitive while protecting our delivery commitments. Proposal (summary):

1) Commercial options
   - 12-month Dedicated commitment (preferred): 3% onboarding credit, unit pricing matched within 5% of Vendor X at your projected volume bands, and a one-time professional services credit to accelerate migration.
   - 6-month bridge: 10% uplift on unit pricing, no onboarding credit.

2) Performance & availability
   - SLA: p95 latency commitment for the dedicated pool; if exceeded in a calendar month, we provide sliding credits up to 10% of monthly spend. SLA tied to the dedicated pool configuration we provision for the run.
   - Availability: we commit to a Dedicated pool sized to cover 95% peak during business hours; for sustained overages beyond agreed windows we'll implement automatic fallback routing to a compatible variant and provide credits for any degraded throughput.

3) Bakeoff mechanics
   - Redwood will run the benchmark the week of May 3. We'll publish a pass/fail dashboard and a short report within 48 hours of completion.
   - If Redwood passes per the test harness without exceeding p95/10% gap vs Vendor X, we'll enter an expedited pilot and honor the 12-month commercial terms above.

4) Timeline & ask
   - Please confirm go/no-go for the bakeoff and whether procurement needs an NDA by Apr 27 so we can provision infra by Apr 30.

I attached a concise counter (proposed_terms_RDW_v3.pdf) with language for the SLA and fallback routing. We can iterate quickly on the credit mechanics if you want a separate credit schedule.

If this sounds reasonable, I'll send a DocuSign link for a non-binding letter of intent to lock the timeline and resource commitment.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed_terms_RDW_v3.pdf
